chunks: First: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the 'Hameel' (captives who recognize each other as kin), so he said: 'And what is the Hameel?' I said: 'A woman is taken captive from her land, and with her is a young child, so she says: He is my son, and a man is taken captive, and his brother meets him, so he says: He is my brother, and they recognize each other, and there is no proof for them regarding that except their word.' He said: 'So what do people say from your side?' I said: 'They do not inherit him, because there was not for her proof regarding that, it was only a birth in polytheism.' He said: 'Glory be to God, if she brought her son or her daughter with her, she remained affirming him, and if he recognized his brother, and that was in the soundness of their intellects, they remained affirming that, and one inherits the other.'

Second: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about two men who were Hameel, brought from the land of polytheism, so one of them said to his companion: 'You are my brother,' and they were recognized by that, then they were freed, and they remained affirming the brotherhood, then one of them died, he said: 'The inheritance is for the other, they are believed.'

Third: As for what Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), who said: 'The Hameel does not inherit except with proof,' so it does not contradict the first two narrations, because the meaning in this narration is that we carry it upon Taqiyyah (dissimulation/prudence), because it is consistent with the view of some of the Sunnis.

key_terms.الإِخَاء: Al-Ikha': The state of being brothers or brotherhood.
key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Al-Taqiyyah: Dissimulation or prudence in religious practice, often used to reconcile differing views or avoid danger.
key_terms.الحَمِيل: Hameel: Captives who recognize each other as kin (brothers, father/son) based on mutual testimony.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on inheritance for captives who recognize each other as kin based on mutual testimony without formal proof?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes that 'Hameel' (captives recognizing kinship) can inherit based on mutual testimony without formal proof, a ruling derived from the continuity of their acknowledgment during the era of polytheism. The apparent contradiction with other narrations requiring proof is resolved through Taqiyyah, as the Imam aligned with Sunni jurists who demanded stricter evidence in that context. This highlights the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in applying contextual evidence for inheritance among displaced families.
